editorial:
Imagine starting at a brand new school where nobody knows you, but you have the added challenge of being blind. That is exactly what Jace Newfield is dealing with. At first, the other kids think he is just mean or arrogant, but really, he is just trying to protect himself and find his place. The vibe here is a classic underdog story that feels like a warm hug. It focuses on friendship, grit, and the struggle to be seen for who you actually are rather than just your disability.

You will really love how the movie handles the wrestling scenes because they show how Jace uses his other senses to win. The acting feels genuine, and while the plot is predictable, it still hits all the right emotional notes. Some parts move a bit slow, but the payoff is worth it. If you want a feel-good night, you should try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or renting it on Apple TV for a crisp picture. It is also a great choice to add the Blu-ray to your physical collection if you love family dramas.
endingExplained: In the final act, Jace proves everyone wrong by competing in a major wrestling match. He uses his hearing and touch to outsmart his opponent, winning the respect of his teammates and classmates. The movie wraps up with Jace finally feeling accepted and loved. He stops pushing people away and learns that being vulnerable is actually a strength. It ends on a high note with Jace feeling confident in his new home.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartwarming stories about overcoming the odds.
